title: Among them was a group who guided by truth.
subtitle: In the middle of the failures, the faithful are named
then: After the story of the calf, the Quran pauses to say that among the people of Musa {reward}is a community who guide by truth and establish justice{/reward}. Ibn Kathir links this to 3:113 and 3:199, which describe people of earlier scripture who stand in prayer at night and humble themselves before Allah.
now: When a family, a team or a neighborhood has let you down, it is easy to write off everyone in it. {idea}The Quran does not do that.{/idea} Even in the hardest story, it stops to honor the ones who stayed true.
old: Once a group has failed, everyone in it is the same.
new: Justice means seeing the upright people even among those who went wrong.
try: Think of a group you have written off. Name one person in it who does good, and say something kind about them.

title: Twelve springs from one rock, and shade, and food.
subtitle: Every need provided, and still they wronged themselves

picture.label: What was given in the desert

then: Allah divided the Children of Israel into twelve tribes. When they asked for water, Musa struck a rock and twelve springs burst out, {reward}each group knowing its own place{/reward}. Clouds shaded them and manna and quails fed them. The verse closes: {trap}they did not wrong Us, they wronged themselves{/trap}.
now: You have running water, a fridge with food, a roof when it rains. Then you skip prayer, snap at your mother, scroll past midnight. {trap}None of it harms Allah.{/trap} It only takes from the person you could have been.
old: When I disobey, I am pushing against Allah.
new: Allah gave me everything, and my sins only hurt me.
try: Drink your next glass of water slowly and say bismillah and alhamdulillah for it.

title: Enter humbly, ask forgiveness, and it is yours.
subtitle: A simple instruction at the gate of the city
then: The Children of Israel were told to settle in the city, eat freely, and {idea}enter the gate humbly, asking forgiveness{/idea}. Allah promised to forgive them and increase the doers of good. Ibn Kathir notes this was revealed in Makkah and also discussed in Surat Al-Baqarah.
now: You get the keys to a new apartment, or walk into the first day of a new job. The moment you cross the threshold is a chance. {idea}Walk in saying astaghfirullah and alhamdulillah{/idea}, not just I made it.
old: A new start is something I earned.
new: Every new door is to be entered humbly, asking Allah's forgiveness.
try: The next time you enter your home today, say astaghfirullah once as you step in.

title: They were given a word and changed it.
subtitle: Swapping a simple command for their own version
then: Those who did wrong among them {trap}changed the word that had been told to them{/trap}. Instead of the humble request for forgiveness, they said something else. So a punishment came from the sky for the wrong they were doing.
now: Your parent asks you to apologize to your sister. You say sorry you feel that way. The words are close, but the meaning is gone. {trap}Changing the instruction while pretending to follow it{/trap} is still disobedience.
old: As long as I do something close to what was asked, it counts.
new: Twisting a clear instruction into my own version is a quiet refusal.
try: Pick one thing you were asked to do, by Allah or a person you owe. Do it exactly as asked today.

title: The fish came on the one day they were told to stop.
subtitle: A test, and a clever trick to get around it
then: The town was Aylah, by the sea, according to Ibn 'Abbas. On the day they were forbidden to fish, the fish came openly; on other days, they did not. Ibn Kathir says {trap}they used a trick, an action that seemed legal on the surface{/trap}, to break Allah's command. The verse calls it a test.
now: You would never steal. But you can claim the expense that is technically allowed. You would never lie. But you can word the email so they draw the wrong conclusion. {trap}A loophole is still a choice.{/trap} {idea}Allah sees the intent.{/idea}
old: If it is technically allowed, it is fine.
new: Tricks around Allah's limits fail, because He sees what I meant.
try: Think of one loophole you use. Ask: if I explained my reason to Allah, would I be comfortable?

title: Why bother warning them? So we are excused before Allah.
subtitle: Three groups in the town, and the reason to keep speaking
then: Ibn Kathir says the town split into three: those who broke the rule, those who warned them, and those who did neither. The silent group asked why bother. The advisers answered: {idea}to be free of blame before your Lord, and perhaps they may fear Him{/idea}.
now: Your friend is getting into gambling, or a cousin keeps drinking and driving. Everyone says: they will not listen, leave it. {idea}You do not speak because you are sure it will work.{/idea} You speak because it is right, and because maybe it will.
old: If they will not listen, there is no point saying anything.
new: I give sincere advice to be clear before Allah, and in hope they may change.
try: Think of one person you have stopped advising. Send one short, kind message today.

title: Those who forbade evil were saved.
subtitle: When the reminder was forgotten, the outcome divided
then: When the wrongdoers ignored the reminder, Allah {reward}rescued those who forbade evil{/reward} and seized the wrongdoers. Ibn Kathir notes the silent group is not mentioned. Ikrimah persuaded Ibn 'Abbas that they too were saved, and Ibn 'Abbas gave him a garment for it.
now: Staying out of it can feel like the safe middle. Not part of the wrong, not making waves. {reward}The verse names the ones who spoke up as the ones saved.{/reward} Silence is not as safe as it looks.
old: If I do not join in, I have done my part.
new: Gently standing against wrong is what the verse holds up as saving.
try: When you hear gossip or a cruel joke today, gently change the subject or say that is not fair.

title: When they kept pushing past the limit, they were humbled.
subtitle: The end of those who mocked the boundary
then: When the Sabbath-breakers {trap}went arrogantly beyond what they were forbidden{/trap}, Allah said: be apes, despised. Ibn Kathir explains despised as humiliated and rejected. It came after the trick, the warnings and the forgetting.
now: It starts with one late night, one small lie, one glance you should not take. Then the limit stops feeling like a limit. {idea}The time to stop is while it is still small.{/idea}
old: I can push the line a bit and still come back.
new: Each step past Allah's limit makes the next one easier, so I stop early.
try: Name one line you have been slowly pushing. Step back from it today, even a little.

title: Swift in penalty, and Forgiving, Merciful, in one breath.
subtitle: Warning and hope placed side by side
then: Allah declared that those who kept defying His law and using tricks around it would face hardship until the Day of Resurrection. Then the verse ends: your Lord is swift in penalty, and He is Forgiving, Merciful. Ibn Kathir says {idea}Allah mentions warning and encouragement together so hearts always have hope and fear{/idea}.
now: You might live only on fear: every mistake feels like the end. Or only on hope: nothing you do really matters. {idea}This verse holds both.{/idea} Take sin seriously, and never stop believing He forgives.
old: Either Allah is strict with me, or He is merciful, not both.
new: Allah's justice keeps me careful, and His mercy keeps me from despair.
try: Tonight, name one sin to stay away from and one hope to hold on to.

title: Tested with good and bad, so they might return.
subtitle: Some righteous, some not, and every season a test
then: Allah scattered the Children of Israel into groups, {reward}some righteous{/reward} and some less so. Ibn Kathir says Allah tested them with ease and difficulty, eagerness and fear, well-being and affliction, {idea}so they might turn back to Him{/idea}.
now: A promotion one year, a miscarriage the next. A good scan, then a bad one. {idea}Both seasons carry the same question:{/idea} will this bring me closer to Allah, or further away?
old: Good times mean Allah is pleased, bad times mean He is not.
new: Good and bad are both tests meant to bring me back to Allah.
try: Whatever kind of day you are having, end it with two minutes of quiet dhikr.

title: They grabbed the quick gain and said: we will be forgiven.
subtitle: Sinning on a promise of forgiveness never asked for
then: A later generation inherited the Book and studied it, but {trap}took whatever this low life offered and said: we will be forgiven{/trap}. As-Suddi described judges who took bribes, saying this. Ibn 'Abbas said the covenant they broke included claiming Allah will forgive sins they keep committing without repenting.
now: You know the rule. You break it anyway and tell yourself Allah is Merciful, I will sort it out later. Then the chance comes again, and you take it again. {idea}The home of the Hereafter is better{/idea}, the verse says. Do you not think?
old: Allah is Merciful, so I can keep doing it and ask later.
new: Hoping for forgiveness while planning to repeat the sin is fooling myself.
try: Name one sin you keep excusing with Allah is Merciful. Today, stop once and actually repent.

title: Hold fast to the Book, keep the prayer, nothing is wasted.
subtitle: The reformers whose reward is never lost
then: After describing those who took quick gain, Allah praises the opposite. Ibn Kathir says these are people who {idea}adhere to the Book, follow its commands, avoid its prohibitions{/idea}, and keep the prayer. {reward}Their reward will not be lost.{/reward}
now: Some days you pray quickly and tiredly, read one ayah and close the app. It feels like nothing. {reward}Allah says He does not waste the reward of those who keep at it.{/reward}
old: My small, tired efforts do not count for much.
new: Allah keeps the reward of everyone who holds on to His Book and prayer.
try: Pray your next salah on time, even if it is short. Trust that it is kept.

title: With the mountain overhead, they were told: hold on firmly.
subtitle: A covenant taken with the mountain raised above them
then: Ibn 'Abbas said that when Musa brought the Tablets, {trap}the commands felt heavy and the people did not want to follow them{/trap}. So the mountain was raised over them like a canopy, and they were told to {idea}hold firmly to what was given and remember what is in it{/idea}.
now: You know what you need to change. It feels heavy, so you keep putting it off. Then a scare comes, a lump, a near miss on the motorway, and suddenly it is clear. {idea}Hold on to it now, before the mountain is overhead.{/idea}
old: I will take my faith seriously when I really have to.
new: Guidance is meant to be taken with strength now, not only in a crisis.
try: Choose one teaching you have found heavy. Take one firm step on it today, before life forces you.
